en: Udāna 8.7 Dvidhāpathasutta Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was traveling along the high road among the Kosalans with the Venerable Nāgasamāla as his attendant monk.
Along the way, the Venerable Nāgasamāla saw a forked path.
Having seen it, he said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, this is the path for the Blessed One;
let us go by way of it.
When this was said, the Blessed One said this to the Venerable Nāgasamāla:
“This, Nāgasamāla, is the path;
let us go by this.
A second time also... [and so on]... [the same was said].
A third time, the Venerable Nāgasamāla said this to the Blessed One:
“This, Bhante, is the path;
let us go by way of it.”
A third time, the Blessed One said to the Venerable Nāgasamāla:
"This, Nāgasamāla, is the path;
let us go by this way."
Then the Venerable Nāgasamāla, having set down the Blessed One’s bowl and robes right there on the ground, departed, saying:
"Venerable sir, here are the Blessed One’s bowl and robes.
Then, as the Venerable Nāgasamāla was traveling along that path, bandits emerged from the road and struck him with their hands and feet; they broke his bowl and tore his outer robe to shreds.
Then the Venerable Nāgasamāla, with his alms-bowl broken and his outer robe torn apart, approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side.
Sitting there, the Venerable Nāgasamāla said this to the Blessed One:
"Just now, Bhante, as I was traveling along that road, robbers came out and struck me with their hands and feet on the way; they broke my bowl and tore my outer robe apart."
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“Though he lives alone, wandering together with others,
the man of realized knowledge remains unmixed with worldly folk.”
The wise man abandons evil,
just as a crane leaves a pond that has no milk.
Thus ends the seventh [verse].
